title: Cabin Pressurisation — System Description

issue.reason: Issue C. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: Flight crew description of cabin pressurisation, covering automatic and manual control of the outflow valve, what the cabin altitude and rate indications mean and when the crew takes over.

sections.purpose: This entry describes cabin pressurisation as the flight crew manages it: the automatic schedule, the manual control of the outflow valve and the indications that show which is in command.
sections.description: Cabin pressure is controlled by modulating a single outflow valve against a schedule computed from the cruise altitude and the landing field elevation. In automatic control the crew sets nothing; the schedule takes the cabin up on a rate that is comfortable and brings it down to arrive at the landing elevation shortly before touchdown. The cabin altitude and the cabin vertical speed are shown on the system page, together with the differential pressure and the valve position. Manual control is selected from the overhead panel and gives the crew direct command of the valve with a rocker: forward closes the valve and the cabin descends, aft opens it and the cabin climbs. The valve moves considerably more slowly in manual than in automatic, so a descent flown on manual control has to be planned rather than corrected, and the crew works the cabin ahead of the aircraft rather than following it. The indicated valve position follows the automatic controller and not the valve shaft, which is worth knowing when the two disagree after a manual descent.
sections.crew_procedure: Normal operation requires no crew action beyond confirming that the landing elevation is correct before descent. To take manual control: select MAN on the overhead panel and use the rocker to command the valve, watching cabin vertical speed rather than cabin altitude, because the valve response is slow enough that altitude alone will lead you into an overshoot. Aim to arrive at the landing field elevation with the cabin already settled. Return to automatic control only on the ground unless the procedure directs otherwise.
